ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y_{1}=-x-1$ intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. It has a point of intersection, M($-2$, m), with the graph of the inverse proportional function $y_{2}= \frac{k}{x}$. What is the area of $\triangle MOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \textbf{Solution:} \text{Given the problem, when } x=0, \text{ we have } y=-1, \text{ meaning the coordinates of B are }(0, -1), \text{ thus } OB=1, \]
\[ \text{Since the coordinates of M are } (-2, 1), \]
\[ \text{Therefore, the distance from point M to line OB is } 2, \]
\[ \text{Therefore, the area of }\triangle MOB \text{ is } \frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 2 = \boxed{1}. \]

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y_1=-x-1$ intersects the x-axis at point A and the y-axis at point B. It intersects the inverse proportional function $y_2=\frac{k}{x}$ at point $M(-2,m)$. What is the area of $\triangle MOB$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are coordinate axes; the straight line slopes downward to the right and intersects the x-axis and y-axis at A and B respectively; point M is located on the left side of the y-axis and at the intersection point of the straight line and the inverse proportional function curve; triangle MOB is formed by the origin O, point B on the y-axis, and point M on the left side. Reasoning: The straight line is y_1=-x-1. Let x=0, obtaining B=(0,-1). Point M(-2,m) is on this straight line, so m=-(-2)-1=1, that is M=(-2,1). In triangle MOB, OB is on the y-axis, with length 1; the horizontal distance from point M to the y-axis is 2. Therefore the area is (1/2)×1×2=1.
